findings.problem: These summary fields compress the REMS limit on FDA's enforcement discretion to 'REMS terms that require the Guide', 'a REMS requires it', 'a REMS so provides', 'as a REMS specifies' or 'a REMS with specific Guide requirements', dropping the guidance's qualifier that the REMS must include specific requirements for reviewing or providing the Medication Guide as part of an element to assure safe use.
findings.rationale: Section III.A.2.b (fifth bullet) and Table 1 of FDA's November 2011 guidance withdraw enforcement discretion only for a REMS with ETASU-based requirements for reviewing or providing the Guide; a REMS that merely includes a Medication Guide under 21 U.S.C. 355-1(e)(2) does not by itself do so. orientation[4], retrieval_prompts[9] and worked_examples[2].steps[5] state the qualifier precisely, the shorthand never contradicts them, and the only case it could mis-decide (a REMS that includes a Medication Guide without an ETASU-based requirement to review or provide it, where the drug is dispensed to a healthcare professional for administration) is marginal on Massachusetts facts. Weighed as Low; the criterion passes.

findings.problem: The item says FDA's enforcement discretion for drugs dispensed to healthcare professionals for administration does not extend to a patient or agent request or to REMS terms, but does not also name the two further limits that apply in outpatient administration settings: the first time the drug is dispensed to a healthcare professional for administration, and the first outpatient dispensing after the Guide is materially changed.
findings.rationale: Section III.A.2.b and Table 1 list both limits for outpatient administration settings. orientation[4], comparison_tables[0].rows[5], worked_examples[2].steps[2], retrieval_prompts[9], quick_review[8], decision_logic[4] and timing_deadlines[3] all state them correctly, so the omission in this one exceptions item is a compression rather than a contradiction and would not mislead a candidate who uses the section. Weighed as Low; the criterion passes.

results.summary: KEEP. Every field was checked against current official text. 21 CFR 208.1, 208.3, 208.20(a), 208.24 and 208.26 (eCFR current to 9/14/2026; Part 208 unamended since 2016; FDA's 2023 Patient Medication Information proposal not finalized) support the section's statements on reach to new and refill prescriptions, the authorized dispenser as an individual, dispensing through the dispenser's agent and to the patient's agent at the time of dispensing, the prescriber's patient-specific direction and the unconditional patient-request override, and FDA's content-and-format exemption power with its two non-exemptible requirements. FDA's November 2011 guidance (still listed as final) is presented as nonbinding enforcement discretion, and its circumstances and Table 1 are reproduced accurately. 21 U.S.C. 355-1(a)(1), (e) and (f)(1)-(4) are paraphrased accurately and no pharmacy duty is stated as common to every REMS. The Mifepristone REMS content matches the 09/30/2025 REMS document (the current version on REMS@FDA) item by item: prescriber certification and guidelines, the four pharmacy certification steps and all fourteen Pharmacy Agreement commitments including the 4-calendar-day delivery rule with prescriber confirmation, NDC and lot recording and the transfer limits, Sponsor de-certification, annual authorized-representative verification, 180-day and annual audits, and distributor shipping limits. The section keeps the actors apart correctly: the REMS makes the certified prescriber responsible for the Patient Agreement Form and for ensuring the patient receives the Medication Guide, while nothing in the REMS document displaces 21 CFR 208.24(e), so the dispensing pharmacist still provides the Guide. The clozapine statements match FDA's Drug Safety Communication (removal effective June 13, 2025; no enrollment to order and no eligibility or ANC verification before dispensing; Boxed Warning and new Medication Guide; ANC monitoring recommendation addressed to prescribers). All four practice questions (MA-Q-0092, MA-Q-0106, MA-Q-0402, MA-Q-0403) are answerable from the section and none is contradicted by it or its explanation. Two Low compressions of the enforcement-discretion policy in summary fields are recorded; neither misleads in context. Monitoring notes, not defects: (1) the January 2023 REMS modification is under challenge in Louisiana v. FDA; the Supreme Court's May 14, 2026 stay in No. 25A1207 of the Fifth Circuit's May 1, 2026 order keeps the current REMS operative, but that stay ends automatically if certiorari is denied, so the in-person-dispensing and mail statements should be re-verified whenever that litigation moves; (2) the clozapine communication also advises health care professionals generally to tell patients to seek care for neutropenia symptoms, nonbinding advice outside the section's declared clozapine objective.
